event.title: Over 100 Affected in Central African Republic Gold Mine Collapse
event.canonical_title: Over 100 Affected in Central African Republic Gold Mine Collapse
event.summary: A gold mine collapse in the village of Zamboye, near the Cameroon border, has resulted in over 100 casualties, according to local officials. The disaster occurred at an illegal artisanal mine, and rescue efforts are ongoing as more miners are reported missing or trapped under the rubble. Authorities are concerned that the casualty count may continue to rise as recovery operations proceed.

timeline.summary: The Central African Republic has shut down the Zamboye artisanal gold mine following a landslide that resulted in at least 49 confirmed deaths. Local sources suggest the death toll may be as high as 100, with many miners still unaccounted for.

event_overview.title: About Central African Republic Mining
event_overview.subject: Central African Republic Mining
event_overview.summary: This event concerns the collapse of an artisanal gold-mining site in Zamboye, a village in the Central African Republic’s Nana-Mambéré prefecture near the Cameroon border, on August 18, 2026. Rescue operations and official efforts to establish the cause, operator responsibility, and final casualty count followed; early reporting described a death toll exceeding 100, though figures remained subject to confirmation.

facts.label: Incident date and place
facts.value: The collapse occurred on August 18, 2026, at a low-technology artisanal gold mine in Zamboye, Nana-Mambéré prefecture, near Cameroon.

facts.label: Mining method
facts.value: The affected operation was described as artisanal gold mining, the small-scale and largely manual form of extraction that accounts for much of the country’s gold and diamond production.

facts.label: Regulator and legal framework
facts.value: The Ministry of Mines and Geology oversees national mining policy; mining is governed by the 2024 Mining Code, Law No. 24-008.

facts.label: National sector context
facts.value: Gold and diamonds are the Central African Republic’s principal mineral commodities, but the sector remains substantially informal and has been associated with conflict and illicit trade risks.

facts.label: Why the event has wider significance
facts.value: Artisanal mining is an important source of income in mineral-producing communities: a World Bank project document estimated that roughly 600,000 Central Africans depended on the sector at least partly for income.

event_overview.scope_note: The selected Muninn timeline covers the immediate August 2026 collapse and ensuing mine-closure response, not the full history of Central African Republic mining, all artisanal-mining accidents, or the eventual investigation findings.
